finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete but discards the boolean result, so no authorization is enforced. Any caller can delete any account by id. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which shows the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at line 23, which deletes the account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the handler for DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is attacker-controlled
Account is looked up by the supplied id with no ownership check
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored, so no exception is thrown on denial

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is correct but its result is unused here. assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw but is not called in deleteAccount. No other guard exists in the repository, which contains only this file. closeAccount at line 29 does use assertCanDelete, so the missing enforcement is specific to deleteAccount.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean that is discarded at line 22; assertCanDelete (13-17) throws but is only called in closeAccount (29). No other guards exist in the repo.
verdict.reason: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete as a bare statement, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user regardless of ownership or admin status, unlike closeAccount, which calls assertCanDelete at line 29.
